name: Programming fundamentals
source: Programming uses instructions to tell a computer what to do. Variables store values. Conditionals select a path based on a condition. Loops repeat instructions.

sections.heading: Variables
sections.body: Variables give names to values so a program can use them later.
sections.tip: Choose names that explain what a value represents.
sections.example: For example, a variable named score can store a student's score.

sections.heading: Control flow
sections.body: Conditionals select a path; loops repeat a set of instructions.
sections.tip: Read a condition as a question with a yes-or-no answer.
sections.example: A loop can repeat a welcome message for each student.

name: Mathematics
source: An equation states that two expressions are equal. To solve a simple equation, apply the same operation to both sides. Example: x + 3 = 7, so x = 4.

sections.heading: Keeping the balance
sections.body: An equation states that two expressions have the same value. Apply the same operation to both sides to preserve equality.
sections.tip: Think of an equation as a balanced scale.
sections.example: If x + 3 = 7, subtract 3 from both sides to find x = 4.

name: English
source: The present simple describes routines and general facts. With he, she or it, most verbs take an -s ending. Example: She studies every day.

sections.heading: Everyday routines
sections.body: Use the present simple to talk about habits, routines, and general facts.
sections.tip: With he, she, or it, most verbs take an -s ending.
sections.example: She studies every day. They study every day.
